✶The National Wire✶

1

Iran and the U.S. Trade Fire at Hormuz

Central Command destroyed three Iranian tankers Friday after Guard missiles were fired at two American warships. Tehran says it struck back this morning. Six months in, no sign of settling.

2

Putin Meets American Envoys in Moscow

Three hours with Witkoff and Kushner, called constructive by the Kremlin. Putin ordered a three-day pause on Kyiv; Zelenskyy says Ukraine will hold fire on Moscow in return.

3

Judge Blocks Postal Screening of Mail-In Voters

A federal judge in Massachusetts struck the plan down as unconstitutional. Two dozen state attorneys general had sued.

4

Global Food Prices Highest Since 2022

The U.N. index rose again in August, every category up. Attacks on Black Sea ports have cut Ukrainian wheat exports to about forty percent of last year's pace.

⚑From the Touchline⚑

The Chase Begins Tonight at Darlington
NASCAR: Southern 500, five o'clock. New format — sixteen drivers, ten races, no eliminations, most points at Homestead wins. Hamlin starts a hundred clear of the field.
Bills: a week from today at Houston. The starting line is expected whole; rookie defensive tackle Zane Durant out at least four games. Josh Allen is No. 2 on the league's Top 100.
Jets: same afternoon at Tennessee, and their first look at Robert Saleh since he was let go. Rookie Cade Klubnik is the backup; the kicking job is still open.

☾On This Day☾

September 6, 1901 — 125 years ago this afternoon, President McKinley was shaking hands in the Temple of Music at Buffalo's Pan-American Exposition when Leon Czolgosz reached the front of the line with a pistol under a bandaged hand and fired twice. McKinley died eight days later. Theodore Roosevelt took the oath in a house on Delaware Avenue, two miles from the spot.

✶Question of the Day✶

The Exposition was famous for its electric light — thousands of bulbs, powered by Niagara Falls. Yet the surgeons working on McKinley that evening operated by reflected sunlight. Why? Answer below the fold.

♡Family Today♡

A quiet Sunday and the last unhurried weekend of summer. Nothing on the calendar that can't wait until Tuesday.
Question of the Day: the fair's emergency hospital had no electric light in its operating room. The doctors used a pan to throw daylight onto the table. A brand-new X-ray machine was on display at the same fair and never used — nobody yet knew if it was safe.
